strings.d1.s0.name: Railay West Beach
strings.d1.s0.tips: 15 minutes by longtail boat from Ao Nang (100 THB). A beach between limestone towers, quiet in the morning and a hub for rock climbing.
strings.d1.s1.name: Phra Nang Cave Beach
strings.d1.s1.tips: One of the world's most beautiful beaches. Visit the princess cave (with its phallus offerings), snorkel, and buy food from longtail boats.
strings.d1.s2.name: Railay Viewpoint & Lagoon
strings.d1.s2.tips: A red-earth rope scramble (short but steep). The view is great, and descending to the lagoon takes nerve.
strings.d1.s3.name: Mangrove Restaurant Railay East
strings.d1.s3.tips: Thai dishes at the mangrove's edge. Try the green curry.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ao Nang Sunset Wang Sai
strings.d1.s4.tips: Seafood at the far end of Ao Nang. Watch the sunset, then take the 17:30 longtail back.
strings.d1.b0.name: Tonsai Beach
strings.d1.b0.tips: A hippie climbers' beach. Walk there at low tide, as an alternative to the viewpoint.
strings.d1.b1.name: Krua Thara Seafood Klong Muang
strings.d1.b1.tips: A local seafood favourite in Klong Muang.
strings.d2.s0.name: Four Islands Tour Ao Nang
strings.d2.s0.tips: Longtail (1,000) or speedboat (1,500). The 400 national park fee is extra.
strings.d2.s1.name: Koh Poda
strings.d2.s1.tips: White sand and a towering rock. Snorkel here: it is Ao Nang's postcard view.
strings.d2.s2.name: Chicken Island Koh Gai
strings.d2.s2.tips: A rock shaped like a chicken's head. Snorkel among the fish.
strings.d2.s3.name: Koh Tup Sandbar Lunch
strings.d2.s3.tips: At low tide a sandbar (Talay Waek) joins three islands. Rice lunch included.
strings.d2.s4.name: Phra Nang Cave & Return
strings.d2.s4.tips: The last stop is Phra Nang. Back in Ao Nang at 16:00.
strings.d2.b0.name: Hong Island Tour
strings.d2.b0.tips: Hong's lagoon and a 360° viewpoint. Choose it instead of the Four Islands tour (as long as it isn't on the next day).
strings.d2.b1.name: Ao Nang Night Market
strings.d2.b1.tips: A night market from Friday to Sunday. Try pad thai and mango sticky rice.
strings.d3.s0.name: Hong Island Speedboat
strings.d3.s0.tips: 30 minutes from Ao Nang, in Than Bok Khorani National Park.
strings.d3.s1.name: Hong Lagoon
strings.d3.s1.tips: A hidden lagoon ringed by limestone towers. Go kayaking.
strings.d3.s2.name: Koh Hong Main Beach
strings.d3.s2.tips: White sand and coral. The 360° viewing platform (419 steps) was built in 2019.
strings.d3.s3.name: Koh Hong Picnic Lunch
strings.d3.s3.tips: Included in the tour. Eat on the beach.
strings.d3.s4.name: Koh Lao Lading & Pakbia
strings.d3.s4.tips: A small cove on Paradise Island. Snorkel, then head back at 16:00.
strings.d3.b0.name: Krabi Town Chao Fah Night Market
strings.d3.b0.tips: Riverside evening food stalls in Krabi Town.
strings.d3.b1.name: Tup Kaek Beach
strings.d3.b1.tips: If you skip the tour: a quiet beach north of Ao Nang. Come for the sunset.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tiger Cave Temple Wat Tham Suea
strings.d4.s0.tips: 1,260 steps (steep!). At the top you'll find a Buddha and a 360° panorama. It's cool at 07:00; watch for monkeys and bring water.
strings.d4.s1.name: Krabi Town Breakfast Ruen Mai
strings.d4.s1.tips: A garden restaurant serving Thai and southern dishes.
strings.d4.s2.name: Emerald Pool Sa Morakot
strings.d4.s2.tips: An emerald-green natural pool in the forest (1 km wooden walkway). It lies in Khao Phra Bang Khram, 1 hour by car.
strings.d4.s3.name: Blue Pool
strings.d4.s3.tips: A blue spring where swimming is forbidden, 800 m beyond the Emerald Pool.
strings.d4.s4.name: Klong Thom Hot Springs
strings.d4.s4.tips: Hot spring pools at 40°C in a forest stream, plus a waterfall.
strings.d4.b0.name: Khao Khanab Nam Caves
strings.d4.b0.tips: A longtail ride from Krabi Town. Explore a cave between two rocks and the mangroves, instead of the pool.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ko Klang Village Lunch
strings.d4.b1.tips: Home cooking in a Muslim fishing village. Get there by boat.
strings.d5.s0.name: Phi Phi Speedboat Ao Nang
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes by speedboat (tour about 2,500 THB). The national park fee is 400.
strings.d5.s1.name: Maya Bay
strings.d5.s1.tips: The bay is closed in August and September (coral recovery). Visit Pileh Lagoon instead.
strings.d5.s2.name: Pileh Lagoon & Viking Cave
strings.d5.s2.tips: Swim in the emerald lagoon. See the swiftlet nest cave from outside.
strings.d5.s3.name: Phi Phi Don Tonsai Lunch
strings.d5.s3.tips: Buffet included in the tour, in the island village.
strings.d5.s4.name: Bamboo Island
strings.d5.s4.tips: White sand and snorkelling. Head back at 16:30.
strings.d5.b0.name: Phi Phi Viewpoint
strings.d5.b0.tips: The classic view over two bays, a 20-minute climb. Do it instead of Bamboo.
strings.d5.b1.name: Ao Nang Krua Thara Evening
strings.d6.s0.name: Klong Muang Beach
strings.d6.s0.tips: Ao Nang's quiet neighbour. A resort beach with good swimming.
strings.d6.s1.name: Tub Kaek Beach
strings.d6.s1.tips: An empty beach with views of the Hong islands. It's also the start of the Dragon Crest (Khao Ngon Nak) hike.
strings.d6.s2.name: Lae Lay Grill
strings.d6.s2.tips: A famous hilltop Thai restaurant with sea views, in Ao Nang.
strings.d6.s3.name: Thai Cooking Class Ya's Krabi
strings.d6.s3.tips: A half-day cooking course with a market visit and 5 dishes.
strings.d6.b0.name: Khao Ngon Nak Dragon Crest
strings.d6.b0.tips: A 3.7 km forest climb with cliff and rock views. Do it instead of the beach.
strings.d6.b1.name: Jenna's Bistro Ao Nang
strings.d6.b1.tips: Thai and Western cuisine. Go in the evening, instead of the class.
strings.d7.theme: Ao Nang morning and an easy farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Ao Nang Beach Morning Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Longtail boats in the morning. Take the Monkey Trail to Pai Plong beach.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pai Plong Beach
strings.d7.s1.tips: The Centara cove. Snorkel and look out for monkeys.
strings.d7.s2.name: Café 8.98 Ao Nang
strings.d7.s2.tips: Breakfast and coffee for your farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Krabi Airport Minibus
strings.d7.s3.tips: 40 minutes from Ao Nang. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ao Nang Landmark Night Market Morning
strings.d7.b1.name: Ao Nang Roti Stand
strings.note0: Stay in Ao Nang (Railay is expensive, Krabi Town is quiet). The longtail to Railay costs 100 THB; Grab and scooters are available; the airport minibus costs 150.
strings.note1: May to October is the RAIN season: afternoon downpours, rough seas, some island tours cancelled, and Maya Bay CLOSED in August and September. It's cheap and green, so book morning tours.
strings.note2: Fill in the TDAC digital arrival card; carry cash in THB. Island tours cost 1,000-2,500 plus the 400 park fee; a taverna meal costs 200-400; round up your tips.
strings.note3: Go to Tiger Cave at 07:00 (heat and monkeys), take the 08:00 slot at Maya Bay, and expect the Four Islands to be crowded midday. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and water shoes.
strings.note4: You'll get wet on the morning longtail (bring a dry bag); ATMs are few in Railay.
strings.note5: Southern Thai food: massaman, gaeng som (sour curry), roti and seafood with coconut. Muslim villages serve halal food.
